record.original_question: Classify all finite-type hypersurfaces of a hypersphere in E^{n+2}.

evidence.quote: Problem 2. Classify finite type hypersurfaces of a hypersphere in E^{n+2}.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{E}^{n+2}$ denote the $(n+2)$-dimensional Euclidean space with its standard inner product, and let $S^{n+1}(r) \subset \mathbb{E}^{n+2}$ be a round hypersphere of radius $r$ centered at the origin. Recall the notion of finite-type submanifold introduced by B.-Y. Chen: an isometric immersion $x: M \to \mathbb{E}^{n+2}$ of a connected Riemannian manifold $M$ is said to be of finite type if the position vector admits a finite spectral decomposition
$$x = x_0 + x_1 + x_2 + \cdots + x_k,$$
where $x_0$ is a constant vector in $\mathbb{E}^{n+2}$ and $x_1, \dots, x_k$ are non-constant $\mathbb{E}^{n+2}$-valued maps satisfying $\Delta x_i = \lambda_i x_i$ for pairwise distinct real eigenvalues $\lambda_1, \dots, \lambda_k$ of the Laplace–Beltrami operator $\Delta$ of the induced metric on $M$. The smallest such integer $k$ is called the type of the immersion; in particular $M$ is of $k$-type.

Problem. Classify, up to congruence in $\mathbb{E}^{n+2}$, all finite-type hypersurfaces $M^n$ of the hypersphere $S^{n+1}(r) \subset \mathbb{E}^{n+2}$, i.e., all $n$-dimensional connected hypersurfaces $M \subset S^{n+1}(r)$ that are of finite type when viewed as submanifolds of the ambient Euclidean space $\mathbb{E}^{n+2}$.
artifact.status_search_result: The general classification of finite-type hypersurfaces of a hypersphere in Euclidean space remains open. Only partial results are available: Takahashi characterized 1-type submanifolds as minimal submanifolds of the sphere, and 2-type hypersurfaces have been studied (e.g., Hasanis–Vlachos and others showing they have constant mean and scalar curvatures), with full classifications only under additional curvature or dimension hypotheses. No complete classification covering all types and dimensions has been established.

status_evidence.title: 2-type surfaces in a hypersphere
status_evidence.snippet: Studies 2-type surfaces inside a hypersphere, indicating that classification is treated case by case rather than in full generality.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial classification (in the 2-type case) is available.

status_evidence.title: Local rigidity theorems of 2-type hypersurfaces in a hypersphere
status_evidence.snippet: Local rigidity theorems for 2-type hypersurfaces in a hypersphere, indicating ongoing partial work rather than complete classification.
status_evidence.claim: The classification problem in spheres is approached via local/partial rigidity results.

status_evidence.title: Quadric hypersurfaces of finite type
status_evidence.snippet: Investigates which quadric hypersurfaces are of finite type, a special subfamily of the broader classification problem.
status_evidence.claim: Special subfamilies are classified, but not all finite-type hypersurfaces of a hypersphere.
